fields.value: Saturate the GPU in shared eval serving

Jack Heart (2026-11-15): "ok thatw enough to confirm the direction and proceed and then add a task for trying to saturate the gpu".

Problem: after EXP-73 (#117), one agent process per machine batches checkpoint forwards for separate game processes. On a 4090 with the frozen Manabot 256-game panel it plays 8,131-9,933 games/hour, 1.02-1.06x Manabot's own server, with identical trajectories. The GPU stays about 29% busy as rows per forward rise from 20 to 35 (32 to 64 games at a time), so the limit is on the host, not the GPU. Evidence: EXP-73 checkout scratch/protocol/fair-comparison.txt and fair-1-evidence/; history in scratch/exp-73-group-an-experiment.md; survey in EXP-66 scratch/shared-inference-survey.md.

Additional observations from `tla_trophies_colab_500k_v2` (2026-11-26, scaling toward 10–100M models):
- `_run_agents` (`src/etude/eval/batching.py:213-238`) runs socket `recv`, `ForkingPickler.loads`, `forwards.answer`, `ForkingPickler.dumps`, and `send_bytes` serially on one thread, leaving the GPU idle during pickling and collation.
- `divide_cpus` (`src/etude/eval/resources.py:129-148`) caps `games <= max_batch` (default 32) assuming 1 input per worker process, which both starves head-to-head batches (at most ~16 per checkpoint at default 32) and forces spawning 128–256 Python processes (~32–64 GiB RAM) to fill a 128–256 GPU batch. Decoupling game-process count from `max_batch` (so multi-game workers sending `len(inputs) > 1` per `Forward` call, like `manabot` MTG-497's concurrent 4-game pairings, can fill `max_batch=128–256` with far fewer OS processes and socket round-trips) directly relieves the host RAM and IPC bottleneck.

Outcome: large-checkpoint GPU eval throughput rises well past the #117 baseline, toward a busy GPU, without changing the author API (`Agents(load=, build=)`, `play(match, agents)`) or the identical-trajectory guarantee.

Start by attributing agent-process host time per forward (input stacking, transfer, sampling, replies, queue wait) and one cell above 64 games at a time. Candidates, chosen by measurement: overlap preparing the next batch and socket IPC with the current forward (pinned buffers, CUDA streams, reader/writer threads), decoupling worker count from `max_batch` for multi-row workers, several batchers or agent processes per GPU, larger concurrency, and filling freed slots across grouped eval jobs to shorten the 21-24 s tail. Priorities (loose, Jack Heart): large-model GPU perf, then client API simplicity, then small CPU perf, then prior art.

Constraints: AGENTS.md; each measurement round at most 30 minutes of rental; ask for a dollar allowance before renting. Starts after #117 lands. No release.
